reason: EBS VolumeLimitCalculator is a self-contained bash script with a documented run command that works offline on CPU.
demo: EBS/VolumeLimitCalculator/Readme.md: install bc, chmod +x and run ./volume_Limit_calculator.sh
goal: Get EBS/VolumeLimitCalculator/volume_Limit_calculator.sh running as the README describes (needs the bc package installed). It reads answers from stdin (volume type, then size/IOPS/throughput) and prints the maximum available IOPS and throughput. It must work for gp3, io2 and st1 inputs fed via stdin.
check: The hidden test pipes several volume configurations into the script and checks the printed IOPS and throughput figures match the expected values.

revision.by: fairness review (every maintained-set exam re-checked against the source)
issues: io1 assertion expects 'throughput is 2500.00 MiB/s' but the script caps io1 <=32000 IOPS at 500 MiB/s (min(500, 2500.00) -> 500); a correct install always fails
io1 isn't in the goal's list of volume types; v2 keeps it with the corrected value, adds the gp3 blank-answer defaults (3000/125) and anchors the matches
evidence: EBS/VolumeLimitCalculator/volume_Limit_calculator.sh:174-187 - io1 max_available_throughput=500 when IOPS<=32000, baseline=min(500, IOPS/4)
data/runs/awslabs-aws-support-tools/result.json audit evidence_out - io1 prints 'Maximum Available throughput is 500 MiB/s'
